explain.say: Here is the secret. Problems has two meanings. Maths problems are sums to solve. Worry problems are things that make you sad. The book has lots of sums, so it is sad. Ha! Well done! Your challenge: find another word with two meanings.

faq.q: Why do I not understand some jokes?
faq.a: Many jokes play with words that have two meanings. Your brain may hear the first meaning, which is perfectly fine. Once you know the second meaning, it clicks.
Usually people laugh at the joke, not at you. Look for friendly faces. If you are not sure, you can ask a friend or a grown-up you trust.

faq.q: What can I say if I do not get a joke?
faq.a: You can say, Can you explain the joke? or I do not get it. Most friends are happy to explain.
asks: Tell me about Can you explain?

faq.q: Why is the maths book joke funny?
faq.a: Problems means sums in maths, and also worries. A maths book is full of problems, so the joke says it must be sad.

faq.q: Do I have to laugh at every joke?
faq.a: No. Not every joke is funny to everyone. A smile, or saying, That is a clever one, is fine.

facts: A joke that plays with a word's two meanings is called a pun.
Many English words have more than one meaning, like bat, bark and problem.
